Subject: Reserved capacity disruption: evidence handoff and scheduling a post-incident sync

Samir —

Thanks again for the quick signal this morning. We observed a reserved GPU pool throughput collapse for your eu-west-1-reserved-012 pool between 08:48–09:02 PT. Impact summary: successful request rate for your svc-frontend fell ~67% and tail latency increased to ~3.4s for a subset of keys.

Immediate notes:
- Root-cause work is ongoing; initial telemetry points at an autoscaler warmup lock amplification that caused a transient eviction wave with associated KV-cache misses.
- We’ve collected server-side allocator traces and prefix-level traces and are attaching an evidence bundle: pulse_log_20250915.zip (high-level events) and allocator_trace.txt (low-level traces).

Requested from you:
1) Confirm impact window and the highest-severity customer tenants you’d like prioritized for rollback/mitigation.
2) Share the internal incident ID you’re tracking so we can align notes (we’ll reference this in our RCA).

Next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll produce a short timeline and meeting packet by EOD today and propose times for a post-incident sync.
- Temporary mitigations applied: increased pool headroom, disabled aggressive warmup coalescing and temporarily tightened preemption thresholds.

I’ll follow up once we have the timeline and a proposal for a credit path.

Attachments: pulse_log_20250915.zip (summary), allocator_trace.txt (raw)

—
Rachel Kim
Customer Success, Dedicated Capacity

Samir —

Appreciate the ORB-INC id. Attached I’ve added the warmup metrics CSV (warmup_metrics.csv) and an evidence_manifest.json that maps the traces to timeline buckets. High-level preliminary timeline (short):
- 08:47:12 PT — autoscaler initiated parallel warmup attempts for 6 nodes in pool reserved-012; 2 nodes reported extended warmup > 45s.
- 08:48:01 PT — warmup coalescing triggered; a lock contention increased scheduler latency.
- 08:48:21 PT — eviction wave begins; KV cache misses spike causing tokenization and latency amplification.
- 08:50–09:02 PT — customer-facing errors observed; mitigation (increased headroom) applied 08:55 PT.

Preliminary cause (engineering hypothesis): an interaction between our warmup coalescing heuristic and a pathological sequence length distribution in your workload produced sustained warmup durations and a small number of driver-side OOM restarts that briefly reduced available capacity. We’ll confirm with the allocator traces.

Credit proposal: as an interim offer we propose a time-proportionate credit covering 50% of the impacted window (08:48–09:02) applied as account credit. We will finalize the precise credit calculation after the postmortem when we have exact token counts and affected tenant lists.

Proposed sync windows:
- Thu 2025-09-18 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET
- Fri 2025-09-19 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET

Ben will follow with a technical deep-dive packet and action owners.

Attachments: warmup_metrics.csv, evidence_manifest.json

—
Rachel
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <ops@orbitalai.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity disruption: evidence handoff and scheduling a post-incident sync

Samir / team —

I’m sharing a short technical readout ahead of the postmortem. Key items:
- Root cause (TL;DR): race amplification in the warmup coalescer + transient driver restarts. The coalescer aggregates warmup for nodes that require similar model weights; under a skewed request distribution it held a scheduler lock longer than expected, allowing allocator queues to back up and triggering eviction heuristics. When a subset of nodes briefly restarted (driver), the pool entered reduced-capacity state and autoscaler attempts to spin replacements were slower due to the same warmup pressure.

Immediate remediation we’ve applied and will push to stable in 48–72 hours:
1) Raise warmup coalescer soft-timeout from 10s -> 25s to avoid holding locks during heavy I/O.
2) Add backoff to autoscaler warmup attempts to prevent parallel warmups for replacement nodes.
3) Increase default pool headroom for reserved-012 from 5% -> 12% until we ship the coalescer fix.

Action owners and ETA:
- BEN: implement coalescer timeout change and autoscaler backoff (PR in review, ETA 36 hours).
- KIM: extend monitoring dashboards and add a synthetic warmup test (ETA 72 hours).
- MARISSA: coordinate communication and billing credit path with Commercial & Finance (ETA 48 hours).

I propose the postmortem call on Fri 2025-09-19 10:00 PT; agenda will be timeline, full RCA, credit calculation, and verified mitigations.

Related: JIRA SUP-3219 created with traces and repro steps. Link: JIRA:SUP-3219

—
Ben Carter
